content: 1. Travica N, Ried K, Sali A, Scholey A, Hudson I, and Pipingas A (2017) conducted a systematic review published in Nutrients (9(9)) to investigate the relationship between vitamin C status and cognitive function. Their findings highlight the potential role of vitamin C in maintaining cognitive health. 2. Tuomilehto J, Lindstrom J, Eriksson JG, Valle TT, Hamalainen H, Ilanne-Parikka P, et al. (2001) demonstrated in the New England Journal of Medicine (344(18):1343–1350) that lifestyle modifications can effectively prevent the onset of type 2 diabetes mellitus in individuals with impaired glucose tolerance. 3. The United Nations (2019) outlined the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) on their official website, emphasizing global efforts to achieve sustainable development by addressing health, education, and environmental challenges. 4. The US Department of Health and Human Services (2004) published a comprehensive report on the health consequences of smoking, detailing its significant impact on public health and the associated risks of chronic diseases. 5. Veronese N, Facchini S, Stubbs B, Luchini C, Solmi M, Manzato E, et al. (2017) conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis published in Neuroscience & Biobehavioral Reviews (72:87–94), which revealed that weight loss is associated with improvements in cognitive function among overweight and obese individuals. 6. Weiss J, Kerfoot A, Freeman M, Motu'apuaka M, Fu R, Low A, et al. (2016) systematically reviewed the benefits and harms of treating blood pressure in older adults. Their findings, published in the VA Evidence-Based Synthesis Program Reports, provide critical insights into hypertension management in aging populations. 7. Wengreen H, Munger RG, Cutler A, Quach A, Bowles A, Corcoran C, et al. (2013) explored the effects of dietary patterns, such as the DASH and Mediterranean diets, on age-related cognitive changes in the Cache County Study on Memory, Health, and Aging. Their results were published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition (98(5):1263–1271). 8. Whitmer RA, Sidney S, Selby J, Johnston SC, and Yaffe K (2005) identified midlife cardiovascular risk factors as predictors of dementia in late life. Their study, published in Neurology (64(2):277–281), underscores the importance of early prevention strategies. 9. The World Health Organization (WHO) (1992) released the ICD-10 classification of mental and behavioral disorders, providing clinical descriptions and diagnostic guidelines to standardize mental health diagnoses globally. 10. WHO (2011) published a report on the global tobacco epidemic, emphasizing the dangers of tobacco use and advocating for stronger public health measures to reduce its prevalence. 11. WHO (2012) provided global estimates on hearing loss prevalence among individuals aged 65 and older, highlighting the significant burden of hearing impairment in aging populations. 12. WHO (2014) released the Global Status Report on Alcohol and Health, which detailed the harmful effects of alcohol consumption and its contribution to the global burden of disease. 13. WHO (2017a) introduced the Global Action Plan on the Public Health Response to Dementia (2017–2025), outlining strategies to reduce dementia risk and improve care for affected individuals. 14. WHO (2017b) published 10 Facts on Dementia, summarizing key information about the condition, its impact, and prevention strategies. 15. WHO (2019a) provided updated guidelines on the management of substance abuse, with a focus on alcohol, to address its public health implications. 16. WHO (2019b) presented data on global obesity trends through the Global Health Observatory, emphasizing the rising prevalence of obesity as a major risk factor for non-communicable diseases. 17. WHO (2019c) reported on raised cholesterol levels as a global health concern, highlighting its role in cardiovascular disease and the need for effective management strategies. 18. WHO (2010) developed a global strategy to reduce the harmful use of alcohol, advocating for policy interventions and public health initiatives to mitigate its impact. 19. Wilson BS, Tucci DL, Merson MH, and O'Donoghue GM (2017) published findings in The Lancet (390(10111):2503–2515) on global hearing healthcare, offering new perspectives on addressing hearing loss worldwide. 20. Wong WB, Lin VW, Boudreau D, and Devine EB (2013) conducted a meta-analysis of observational studies on the use of statins in preventing dementia and Alzheimer’s disease. Their findings, published in Pharmacoepidemiology & Drug Safety (22(4):345–358), assessed potential confounding factors. 21. Wu L and Sun D (2017) reviewed adherence to the Mediterranean diet and its association with reduced risk of cognitive disorders. Their systematic review and meta-analysis were published in Scientific Reports (7:41317). 22. Wu L, Sun D, and Tan Y (2017) examined the relationship between fruit and vegetable intake and the risk of cognitive disorders. Their findings, published in the Journal of Nutrition, Health & Aging (21(10):1284–1290), support dietary interventions for cognitive health. 23. Xu WL, Atti AR, Gatz M, Pedersen NL, Johansson B, and Fratiglioni L (2011) demonstrated that midlife overweight and obesity increase the risk of late-life dementia in a population-based twin study published in Neurology (76(18):1568–1574). 24. Xu W, Tan L, Wang HF, Jiang T, Tan MS, Tan L, et al. (2015) conducted a meta-analysis of modifiable risk factors for Alzheimer’s disease, published in the Journal of Neurology, Neurosurgery & Psychiatry (86(12)). 25. Xu W, Wang H, Wan Y, Tan C, Li J, Tan L, and Yu JT (2017) analyzed the dose-response relationship between alcohol consumption and dementia risk. Their meta-analysis of prospective studies was published in the European Journal of Epidemiology (32(1):31–42). 26. Yaffe K, Falvey C, Hamilton N, Schwartz AV, Simonsick EM, Satterfield S, et al. (2012) investigated the effects of diabetes and glucose control on cognitive decline over nine years in older adults without dementia. Their study was published in Archives of Neurology (69(9):1170–1175). 27. Zhang Y, Chen J, Qiu J, Li Y, Wang J, and Jiao J (2016) conducted a dose-response meta-analysis of fish and polyunsaturated fatty acid intake and the risk of cognitive impairment. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition (103(2):330–340). 28. Zheng Y, Fan S, Liao W, Fang W, Xiao S, and Liu J (2017) performed a meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies on hearing impairment and Alzheimer’s disease risk. Their results were published in Neurological Sciences (38(2):233–239). 29. Zhong G, Wang Y, Zhang Y, Guo JJ, and Zhao Y (2015) found that smoking is associated with an increased risk of dementia. Their meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies was published in PLOS One (10(3):e0118333). 30. Zhou S, Zhou R, Zhong T, Li R, Tan J, and Zhou H (2014) examined the association between smoking, alcohol consumption, and dementia risk among elderly men in China. Their study was published in Current Alzheimer Research (11(9):899–907).
